subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: History and culture through performing arts
altText: Basic 3 learners watching a video of a Ghanaian festival and discussing its music, dance and costumes.
detailedDescription: In a Basic 3 classroom, a short video of a Ghanaian festival plays on a TV or projector, showing drumming, dancing, chiefs and colourful costumes. Learners sit in small groups with simple note sheets, pointing at the screen and discussing what they see. The teacher guides them to notice instruments, movements and how the performance honours the people’s history and culture.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 pupils examining photos of music, dance and drama performances from different parts of Ghana.
detailedDescription: Basic 3 learners gather around a table covered with photos of different Ghanaian performing artworks: traditional dance groups, drama scenes, choirs and poetry recitals. They point at different pictures and talk about costumes, instruments, props and where such performances may happen. The teacher writes key words like ‘festival’, ‘wedding’ and ‘storytelling’ on a chart to help them compare performances across communities.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Environment as source of sound and movement
altText: Basic 3 learners walking around the school compound, observing and noting everyday sounds and movements.
detailedDescription: Basic 3 pupils move around the school compound with small notebooks. They point to birds flying, leaves rustling, a passing trotro, children skipping rope and the distant sound of a church bell. Some children write short notes or draw quick symbols to represent sounds and movements. The teacher reminds them to listen carefully and feel rhythms they might later turn into music, dance or drama.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Topical issues as themes for performing arts
altText: Basic 3 children in a circle discussing pictures of flooding, fires and road accidents as ideas for songs, dances and dramas.
detailedDescription: Inside the classroom, Basic 3 learners sit in a circle with pictures showing topical issues like flooding, domestic fires, poor waste disposal and unsafe roads placed in the middle. They point to each image and discuss what the problem is and how a song, dance or drama could encourage people to change. The teacher writes short idea phrases on a manila sheet, emphasising that performing arts can address serious community concerns.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Experimenting with sound, voice and movement
altText: Basic 3 learners in small groups clapping, stamping, tapping bottles and exploring body movements.
detailedDescription: Small groups of Basic 3 pupils explore different sound and movement possibilities in a classroom. One group claps patterns and stamps their feet, another taps plastic bottles and tins like drums, while a third group experiments with simple body movements and gestures. The teacher moves between groups, asking them to vary speed and loudness and to listen carefully to each other.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Creating short performing pieces from ideas
altText: Basic 3 pupils planning and rehearsing short songs, dances or drama scenes using large planning sheets.
detailedDescription: Seated in groups, Basic 3 learners plan short performances using large sheets divided into ‘Beginning’, ‘Middle’ and ‘Ending’. They draw stick figures and write short phrases to show how their piece will flow. Some children rehearse short rhythm or dialogue sections while others refer to the plan. The teacher encourages them to link their story to real Ghanaian community experiences.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 learners practising a short performance while a classmate observes and gives simple feedback.
detailedDescription: A small group of pupils rehearses a short performance in a classroom or open space. One learner leads a song line while others respond, and a pair act out a simple dialogue with clear gestures. A classmate stands aside holding a feedback card with simple symbols, ready to suggest improvements like ‘speak louder’ or ‘stand closer’. The teacher allows the children to correct timing and positions themselves.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 learners designing simple costumes and props from local materials for their performances.
detailedDescription: Basic 3 learners sit around a table covered with scraps of cloth, cardboard, paper, masks and small sticks. They sketch costume and prop ideas on paper and hold materials up to their bodies or faces to imagine how they will look on stage. The teacher reminds them that costumes and props must be simple, safe and respectful of cultural meanings. The scene shows resourceful, low-cost creative planning.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 class planning a simple performance event using a chart on the board.
detailedDescription: In the classroom, a chart on the board shows columns like ‘Who performs?’, ‘What?’, ‘Where?’ and ‘When?’. Basic 3 learners raise their hands, suggesting groups and items such as songs, dances and short dramas. Two pupils stand at the board, writing names and performance titles. Another group looks at a rough floor plan of the classroom or compound, deciding where performers and audience will sit or stand.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 pupils presenting a short performance to classmates and a few parents in the school compound.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian school compound, a group of Basic 3 learners perform a planned piece combining song, movement and short dialogue. They wear simple, safe costumes and use basic props. Classmates sit as the main audience, with one or two parents standing at the back watching. The atmosphere is respectful and joyful as children show what they have created for their school community.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 pupils watching a replay of their performance on a tablet and looking at printed photos.
detailedDescription: After the event, a few Basic 3 learners watch a short video recording of their performance on a tablet or phone held by the teacher. Other children look at printed photos of key moments pinned on a classroom board. Some pupils write very short notes like ‘We forgot this part’ or ‘Audience clapped here’. The focus is on documentation as a tool for learning and improvement, not on social media.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 class in a feedback circle discussing strengths and improvements after a performance.
detailedDescription: Basic 3 learners sit in a circle after a performance. In the centre is a chart labelled ‘What we did well’ and ‘Next time we will…’. A pupil from the audience holds a ‘talking object’ and gives kind feedback to the performing group. A performer listens respectfully. The teacher writes some comments on the chart, modelling how to give specific, encouraging feedback instead of harsh criticism.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 learners filling out simple reflection sheets about how they performed and what to improve.
detailedDescription: At their desks, Basic 3 pupils quietly complete reflection sheets after a performance. The sheets include prompts such as ‘I enjoyed…’, ‘I found difficult…’ and ‘Next time I will…’. Some children draw small self-portraits on stage, while others write short sentences. The teacher walks around, helping each learner decide on one practical improvement goal for future performances.
